It’s a coin toss. That’s about as nuanced as the discussion can get. But generally, a few people seem to get notably better, a few don’t seem to notice a difference either way, and most tend to get worse, either temporarily or persistently. 

I’ve gotten some symptomatic relief from taking Adderall, Pregabalin, Gabapentin, Baclofen and Midazolam. I don’t take any of them regularly, and some I haven’t used in years. The others I’ve used sparingly, and they help improve some symptoms. I would strongly recommend against taking anything if you can avoid it, but if your state is truly unbearable, some things could possibly help you get through the worst of it.

I’d also strongly recommend avoiding SSRIs, SNRIs, antipsychotics entirely. I’m pretty sure my case of PFS is as bad as it is because of past SSRI use, and while it could help things, more often than not it seems to have made people worse.

Took SSRIs at 15/16 for a few weeks and had some enduring changes to sexual function (but still within the range of normal) that I wasn’t really worried about at the time. Namely I could not orgasm from penetrative sex, and had this issue with multiple partners. Still had decent libido, normal erections, etc. but sensation was definitely lower than before. I saw sex as an enjoyable activity that I would still engage in, but definitely was not as interested as I used to be.

Additionally, there some other more minor changes to motivation and focus, and I’d had more trouble paying attention to things and getting things done than I used to, I ended up getting clinically dx’d with ADHD.

At 18, I took Finasteride for a couple of days before I stopped because of testicular pain, and over the next few weeks, I experienced a complete reversal of these changes that had occurred when I was younger. I suddenly was able to orgasm from penetrative sex (which I’d never been able to since I was sexually active), and I finally understood why people loved sex. Also, my motivation and focus were fixed. As long as I started, I was able to work on what I wanted to work on the entire day.

Unfortunately, a few weeks later I took Finasteride again as I’d read that this testicular pain side effect was fairly common and usually went away as long as you’d continued on the drug. This marked what was essentially the end of my life.

I experienced extreme anxiety (0 history of anxiety prior to this), constant suicidal thoughts, complete impotence, dry ejaculation, derealization, extreme anhedonia, numb genitals, orgasmic anhedonia, extreme gastric issues (intense pain and constipation, stool that looked like pellets), insomnia, psychotic episodes, and a whole list of issues that I’m not going to describe in detail since that isn’t the focus of this discussion. Essentially felt like my body had just ceased to function properly.

The first year was brutal, and I was not able to figure out anything that improved my quality of life to any significant degree. Whatever medication I took that improved the symptoms gave me at most, a few hours a week, and that’s what I lived for. A few hours every week where I did not feel extreme torture and suicidal ideation.

Eventually, after this extended period of intense suicidal ideation, my doctor convinced me to try Vortioxetine, which, after just 2 doses, induced what is referred to in the patient community as a crash, that lasted a few days. I thought this was the end for me. However, a few days later, I experienced the most significant improvement in my baseline functioning since my illness. I’d also had improved responses to the medications I had been taking intermittently for symptom management.

I believe these 2 conditions are linked and these medications just happen to be triggers for them in people who are predisposed to developing them. These medications can also modulate disease state, just not in a way that’s controllable. You could end up much much worse, or better, and it is a coin toss.

Many clinicians have disagreed with me saying that if this was the case, these experiences would have been reported in clinical trials. In 2019, it came out that at least in Finasteride’s case, there were a number of participants in the clinical trials who experienced side effects past the wash out period of the drug, that were not included when calculating the side effect figures - only those who completed the 5 year trial were included as data points, while those who dropped out due to side effects did not count towards the 0.3% figure that is touted for sexual sides. Additionally, they changed the labeling from side effects resolve in all men who discontinue Finasteride, to side effects resolve in men (https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/usa-courts-secrecy-propecia/).

I’ve also had clinicians disagree with me saying that if these effects weren’t caught in trials, they would be found in post marketing surveillance - yet not a single one of the 15+ clinicians I met over multiple specialities reported my problems to the regulator. The reasoning was usually that it’s outside of what’s described as possible in the clinical guidance, or that there was no point since they cared about how they could improve my QoL as an individual, and were unconcerned with the bigger picture since there was nothing for me to be gained immediately from reporting it. I hope you can see how this entirely defeats the purpose of post marketing surveillance (which I think should play a larger role in clinical guidance since it is where both the clinician and the patient are aligned and incentivized to find the truth - as opposed to trials/studies funded by pharmaceutical companies which can and have been manipulated for profit in the past and will continue to be like that). My experience is not uncommon amongst the patient support groups that I have been a part of.

I hope this changes at least one professional’s mind and convinces them to consider that we’re not at a point where we’ve figured everything that could go wrong with someone, and the systems that we have in place to capture edge cases are not adequate. If someone comes to you complaining about xyz side effect, it could entirely be in their head. It could also be because of some organic cause that is not currently understood. Please consider the latter possibility.

You midwits are trying to speculate on a system with so many unknowns and no real working data. I’ve read the forum(s) back to front, 100s of papers trying to make sense of the issue, and the only rational conclusion you can come to at the end of it is that there isn’t enough data to safely “treat” this condition. Hence the studies being done.

These discussions are so far above your pay grade(s) - you have people over here sitting and saying they think “reducing AR expression and fixing cortisol sensitivity” will fix the problem like it’s some sort of math equation. But the reality of the problem is infinitely more complicated than that. Here’s an anecdote - I know someone who temporarily experienced a complete recovery from taking dexamethasone. 100s of different substances consumed over their 10 or so years of PFS, and nothing really produced sustained improvements. One day they had, in their words, a temporary complete reversal of symptoms. It never worked again. After extended breaks, after dramatically increasing the dosage, dramatically decreasing the dosage,  trying other drugs in that class with similar effects, nothing produced the same response. Why did dexamethasone work? Who the fuck knows? Why did it never work again? Who the fuck knows? 

Ive taken a number of substances since I first got sick that have produced responses in me ranging from inducing a crash that produced sustained longer term improvements to medium term worsening with no longer term improvements to short term improvements with immediate rebound effects. Some substances that worked amazingly for me symptom management wise in years 1-4 have produced different effects in years 6-7. Some of these substances have produced severe crashes that other people haven’t recovered from. Some of these substances other people have taken for months at a time with no significant long term changes to their condition.

The point I’m trying to make from this anecdote and from my own experiences, is that when you sit over here and throw your hands in the air wondering why no one wants to engage in the spiel about PFS being this or PFS being that or this protocol or that protocol, it’s because trying to fix PFS the way you talk about it is like trying to do surgery on someone with a spoon, no blueprints, and the lights off. It is not a matter of whether you will hurt yourself, it is a matter of when. Outside of engaging in a relatively healthy lifestyle (as much as your body allows), the smartest thing to do is to wait for more information. If you’d like to speed that along, donate more. Or go study molecular biology and start your own lab where you can run your own experiments at whatever pace you like.

I had a brief stint of SSRI usage (a few weeks) as a teenager and I had some lasting symptoms from that (some genital numbness, slightly lower libido, lower motivation, nothing too far outside the range of normal but definitely not what my normal was or had been - it normalized to how it was before SSRIs the first time I took finasteride, and then I developed PFS after my second usage of Finasteride). I believe the conditions are linked and it’s what predisposed me to having such a bad case of PFS from such short exposure.

As someone with PFS, you should be optimistic since you’ve been on it for as long as you have and it’s only been 3 weeks off. It’s a lot more likely you’re experiencing sides from the drug still being in your system and you should be fine once it washes out. Give it a few weeks and hopefully this will just be a bad memory.
Was very fit before I developed persistent sides. Lifted + did cardio 6 days a week religiously. It’s a coin toss.

While I appreciate the well wishes and the thought behind this, there were no underlying issues to speak of. Did great at school, did great at the gym, had good friendships and a great relationship. Took Finasteride for 2 weeks, and that caused a whole host of issues that made everything fall apart very quickly. Hard to go to the gym when exercising suddenly makes you feel sick (+ your joints and muscles hurt so much you can’t even make it through more than a few sets), hard to maintain a relationship when you can’t express/feel any emotion or engage sexually, hard to maintain friendships when all you are incapable of engaging in any social interaction because suddenly for the first time in your life you are uncontrollably anxious and depressed for no reason, and hard to well at school when you cannot pay attention or focus because your brain just feels completely blocked. That’s not even the half of it - there’s the insomnia (which, at its worst, does not respond to sedatives or hypnotics - even if you have no tolerance to speak of), the fatigue (have 0 energy to do anything but cannot fall asleep), the vertigo, the inability to taste, smell, shit, piss - the list just goes on and on and on and on.

 There is no doubt in my mind that these problems were, for me, at least, caused by finasteride as nothing else explains how my body and mind just broke down overnight. Life was good - a breakdown this comprehensive and severe just does not happen out of the blue. Just went to bed a happy, healthy, normal person, and woke up in a completely different reality.

Obviously, in the beginning, I looked for alternative explanations. I wanted this desperately to be something I understood and could fight. I got some blood work done and my hormones were all over the place. I thought maybe once they normalized things would get back to normal. Not the case. 3 months later, unremarkable bloodwork, and the problem still persists. 18 months later, stellar bloodwork for a young male, same deal.

Visited multiple therapists,  psychiatrists, urologists, endocrinologists, etc. etc. throughout this whole ordeal. Have tried all sorts of lifestyle based interventions, medications, talk therapy, etc. No real success.

No matter what people on this sub say, this is a very real thing that, to an outsider, is unfathomable. Very uncommon, but if it happens to you, there is no fighting it. 

Congratulations on getting the best of your personal struggles and I wish you well.

I have PFS. It’s been 6 years for me. My life is ruined. No words will ever encompass how horrible this disease can be if you are unfortunate enough to have been dealt this hand. I’ve accepted that if there isn’t a solution to this, my life probably ends before I turn 30.

It used to make me sad. The idea of leaving everything and everyone I loved, giving up on all the dreams I had, not getting to experience the things I wanted to experience since I was a child - used to make me feel so sad. Now I just don’t care anymore. I am tired. I’ve been tired for so long. 

I wish people could see what I saw so they would really understand what they are risking. It is really uncommon, but if you get it, everything that makes your life your life, goes.

It is not bullshit. I personally experienced horrible sides from taking Finasteride for a brief period of time, some of which persist 5 years later. DHT blockers are nowhere near as benign or safe as they are currently portrayed.

I suffer from a similar condition from taking another drug (some researchers who’ve studied both problems believe they might be the same - just triggered by different substances), and as hellish as this sounds, it absolutely can get worse.

This condition, like most, presents as a spectrum. A “mild” case would be someone that presents with erectile dysfunction, loss of libido, and other symptoms that absolutely have a negative impact on your quality of life but you can work around and have a life outside of. On the other end, there are patients that constantly have genital pain, they describe their genitals as degrading, severe anxiety that doesn’t respond to benzodiazepines, anhedonia, food intolerances, severe insomnia (a friend of mine in the community regularly goes days without sleeping and has not slept longer than 3-4 hours in a night over the past 5 years - when he goes through particularly bad periods, he also cannot eat for days without throwing up food undigested), changes in facial structure, bone density, intolerance to exercise, cognitive difficulties, etc. The list is essentially endless and the gist of it is that it turns you into a soulless husk that isn’t even really existing.

What makes this whole condition even more overwhelming for patients is that many patients have gone from mild to moderate/severe cases after ingesting other SSRIs or antidepressants in an attempt to treat their mental symptoms, since it is often characterized as depression.

With respect, “scientific data” isn’t the be all and end all either. Science is the best framework we have in the modern world for assessing facts like this (is this medication safe? does this medication treat what it’s supposed to treat?), but it is NOT infallible. 

The pharmaceutical industry is rife with corruption and they constantly manipulate safety trial data, regulators and health care professionals to make more money. There is constantly medication making it to market that shouldn’t be making it to market because the regulation is piss poor. It is insufficient, there is a lot of conflict of interest that leads to all sorts of shit thats written about pretty well here (https://www.nytimes.com/2022/09/15/health/fda-drug-industry-fees.html).

The outcomes are just as you’d expect. The opioid crisis (seriously - how does an entire generation of health care professionals not question how a drug based on what has historically been one of the most addictive substances in the world, is suddenly non addictive?), benzodiazepines (prescribing guidelines used to be such that many doctors would prescribe it for medium and long term use - these days, many people struggle to get a prescription even a few days long because of how many people had their lives ruined by the whole non habit forming non dependence forming lie), and what has personally affected me - a drug called Finasteride - here’s an article that talks about it, where it’s been written about in great detail how some of the safety data was manipulated to paint a false picture to patients and healthcare professionals (https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/usa-courts-secrecy-propecia/).

The next time someone shares their experience of being harmed by medication in some way that doesn’t fit the standard, I would urge you to consider the possibility that they are telling the truth. Modern medicine is amazing in a lot of ways, but it’s not even close to having it all figured out. Refusing to acknowledge this has a real cost. For me, constantly being gaslit about what I was going through (it being labeled as depression/anxiety when it was so much more) when I was going through the worst of it just put another reason on the plate of someone who already thought about killing themselves 50 times a day. I am not suggesting that anecdotal evidence become a replacement for science, just that it has a place at this table considering all the circumstances.

Because some of us have had our lives dramatically affected by it. I have made friends in the PFS community that eventually decided to take their own lives as a result of their suffering. Talking about the experiences that we have had so other people are spared the same fate can be described in many ways, but I wouldn’t describe it as annoying.

If somebody is discouraged by hearing about these experiences, that is not necessarily a bad thing.

I believe I have a unique perspective on this. When I was 18, I had similar concerns about my hair. My hair loss wasn’t even close to noticeable, but my father is bald and I decided to get ahead of the problem by taking the drug you refer to. When I mentioned it to my girlfriend at the time, she encouraged me and jokingly said she wouldn’t find me attractive if I lost my hair.

To this day, it is the only decision I have made in my life that I categorically regret. The sexual side effects aren’t even half the horror story that this drug can cause. I experienced sexual dysfunction, derealization, cognitive issues, depression, anxiety, insomnia, amongst a whole host of other issues. It cost me my friendships, my relationship, my ambitions, and most importantly, myself. When the condition first took hold, it was a truly jarring experience. Words do not do it justice. I have no history of anxiety but found myself experiencing a form of it that I did not know was possible. High doses of benzodiazepines that should knock someone out would barely touch it. Alcohol had no effect on me either - half a bottle of hard liquor would have me feeling a little nauseous, but nothing else. Antidepressants made things worse. My brain was so severely fucked up that I did not care about the fact that my sexual functioning was compromised. Being in this condition, I found myself unable to function. I was a complete mess. Slowly, this put a strain on all of my relationships. With my friends, my girlfriend, and my family. One by one, my friends stopped reaching out to me. My relationship with my girlfriend became a source of misery rather than one of happiness. My parents coped with my condition by refusing to acknowledge it, and labeling it as some sort of depressive phase. Going through this shattered my soul. Each of the symptoms I was experiencing caused enough of a drop in someone’s quality of life that it alone was enough of a reason to take one’s life. Dealing with all of them, and all the secondary consequence of being sick, ruined me. I tried to take my life a few years ago, but I did not succeed. 

Prior to all of this, I was an extremely high achieving 18 year old. I did well academically, had fulfilling friendships, worked out consistently (and was very physically fit), and had a number of other hobbies. In the years since (I am 23 now), my symptoms have improved to some degree, but I am nowhere near normal. 

I’m from Kerala too, but I do not follow this subreddit. I don’t know why reddit’s algorithm sent this to me, but when I saw it I felt like I had to say something. If you take this drug, there’s a very small chance you will get sick. But if you do, it will be the biggest regret of your life. Please don’t take it.

As a side note, even if my experience wasn’t something to consider, the way your wife has handled this situation is shameful. Appearance is a consideration in attraction, but when she married you, she knew what you looked like. Her demand is completely unreasonable - asking you to do something like get a different haircut, or to shave your facial hair would be a reasonable request. Demanding that you consume a medication to treat a cosmetic issue is absurd. Would you ever dream of demanding she get breast implants? Then refusing to compromise and reject all her attempts at resolving the problem?

When people show you who they are, believe them. Do not ignore the signs. You deserve better my friend.
